title: A cosmic quartet
caption: Galaxy group HCG 86, imaged by ESO's VLT Survey Telescope
celestial: HCG 86 · constellation Sagittarius · about 270 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Four galaxies form a loose triangle in this image from ESO's VLT Survey Telescope, with three in a straight line and one below them. The bright objects just right of the elongated galaxy do not belong to the group. Together the four make up HCG 86, about 270 million light-years from Earth in Sagittarius.

HCG stands for Hickson Compact Group, a name for groups of four to ten galaxies packed very close together. That closeness makes such groups ideal places to study how galaxies interact, sometimes to the point of merging.

This view was made by a team led by Rossella Ragusa of Italy's Istituto Nazionale di Astrofisica. The survey telescope can pick up very faint structures in the outer parts of galaxies, relics of old interactions. By mapping the light in and around the group, the team concluded these faint features are remains of satellite galaxies swallowed by the group around seven billion years ago.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (15.64 x 10.76 arcminutes) and distance (270 million light years), the frame spans roughly 1.2 million × 845,000 light-years. Its light set out about 270 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This visible-light image was taken with the OmegaCAM camera on ESO's VLT Survey Telescope through g, r and i filters. The color assigned to each filter is not published.
filters: 480 nm · Optical g (VLT Survey Telescope OmegaCAM)
625 nm · Optical r (VLT Survey Telescope OmegaCAM)
770 nm · Optical i (VLT Survey Telescope OmegaCAM)
understand.eye: The long exposures gather far more light than the eye, which helps reveal the faint structures in the galaxies' outskirts.

behind.people: See full credit: ESO/Ragusa, Spavone et al.

behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The image is part of the VST Early-type Galaxy Survey, known as VEGAS.

The VST, at ESO's Paranal Observatory in Chile, is one of the world's largest telescopes built to survey the sky in visible light. It marked a decade of operation in 2021, helping search for exoplanets and probe our galaxy and the wider Universe.
alt: Four galaxies arranged in a triangle, three in a row and one below, with some bright objects to the right of the elongated galaxy.
